home_intro: This app demonstrates the FormKrafter stack consumed from React through the generated wrappers: the drag & drop builder, the form renderer, rules and validation.
playground_intro: Build a form with the palette, configure bricks in the property panel, then try it live in the preview below.
playground_preview_hint: Build a form above to preview it here.
ex_simple_intro: The number one production case: a spec saved in your database, rendered with FkFormRender, validated and submitted.
ex_wizard_intro: A stepper with per-step validation, locked step navigation and a final submit button.
ex_i18nform_intro: Labels, options and error messages carry per-locale en/fr values — switch the app language and the form follows, errors included.
ex_remote_intro: Options fetched from a public API with server-side search, plus a second select depending on the first through URL interpolation.
ex_grid_intro: A data grid with per-row validation and a minimum row count — validate to see contacts[0].name style errors.
ex_auth_intro: A token injected through the data prop and referenced as _authToken in the request headers — and provably absent from the submitted payload.
ex_auth_proof: The select options below display exactly what the data source received:
ex_rules_intro: Show, disable and compute fields from other answers — json-logic by default, sandboxed JavaScript when needed. Pick “Other”, tick the checkbox, set quantity above 10.
ex_server_intro: The submitted data is revalidated inside a TanStack server function with validateFormData from the core — compare both verdicts.
ex_custom_intro: A star-rating brick registered at runtime with registerBrick, validated and rendered like any built-in.
ex_fio_intro: Paste a Form.io form definition, convert it with convertFormioForm from the core, and get a live FormKrafter spec — fields, layout, validations and simple conditionals included. Whatever cannot be mapped is listed as a warning.
fio_weight_note: Bonus: migrating roughly halves your gzipped form-stack weight (~214 KB for the full FormKrafter builder vs ~470 KB for formio.full.min.js) and drops the Bootstrap dependency — details and methodology in the docs.
ex_theming_intro: Every FormKrafter style flows through --fk-* CSS custom properties. The same form below, themed six different ways — each card shows the exact code that produces it.
theming_default_desc: styles.css as shipped — it follows the app theme automatically via the .dark class.
theming_css_desc: Override a handful of --fk-* tokens on any ancestor — plain CSS, no build step.
theming_dark_desc: data-fk-theme on a wrapper flips this subtree to dark, whatever the app theme is. Give the wrapper a dark surface so the tokens have the right backdrop.
theming_tailwind_desc: Arbitrary properties let Tailwind set the tokens from your design system, right in the class list.
theming_bootstrap_desc: For the nostalgic: tokens tuned to the Bootstrap defaults. If your host app loads Bootstrap, alias its variables directly.
theming_ant_desc: Same idea with the Ant Design seed tokens — map colorPrimary and borderRadius onto --fk-*.
theming_frameworks_note: No UI framework is loaded on this page: the Bootstrap and Ant cards only remap the --fk-* tokens to those design languages. In an app that already ships one of them, point the tokens at the framework variables — e.g. --fk-color-primary: var(--bs-primary) — and FormKrafter follows its theme.
home_playground_hint: Every example below can also be opened pre-loaded in the playground.
ex_nested_title: Reference a form inside a form
ex_nested_intro: The host form embeds two reusable forms through nested-form bricks: at render time each specRef is resolved by services.specSourceService and inlined — fields, validations and rules included.
ex_nested_note: This page registers an in-memory spec source with two refs (adresse, contact-urgence) and a simulated latency. In production, point fetchSpec at your own form store.
